newsitem.title: POLAND: SOCCER-GASCOIGNE ONLY DOUBT FOR WORLD CUP QUALIFIER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GASCOIGNE ONLY DOUBT FOR WORLD CUP QUALIFIER.

text.p: England manager Glenn Hoddle has still to decide whether or not to start with Paul Gascoigne in his side's vital World Cup qualifier against Poland on Saturday.

"If he is fit, and I think he will be, that is the decision I have to make," Hoddle said on Friday. "I was very impressed with the way he played against South Africa last week, and he has responded well to treatment following the late injury to his calf in that match.
"When I first saw the bruise I thought it would need three or four days treatment but he has been training since Monday and having treatment to get fit.

"My decision is whether to play him fron the start or to bring him on later in the game. We are playing on a huge pitch tomorrow and I think the game will spread out a lot in the last 20 minutes and I must decide on how best to use him. He is the type of player who can win a game with one flash of brilliance and it is a game we must win tomorrow."
He said the only other player in his squad also undergoing treatment was midfielder Paul Ince, who has a knee injury. Ince is certain to play.

Hoddle, speaking on a grim rainy day in the heart of the Silesian coalmining region, stressed his team were hoping to chisel out three points with a victory that would guarantee them second place at least in the group -- which at worst would mean a place in the playoffs if they fail to win the group.

"Our aim is to take three points from this match and three points when we play Italy in October. In fact this game against Poland is bigger than the Italy game because if we don't win here, the Italy situation won't happen."
In the past 24 years the two countries have met in the World Cup finals, three World Cup qualifying competitions and a European qualifying competition.
Poland eliminated England from the World Cup in 1973 and effectively from the European championships in 1991, but have beaten England only once in 11 meetings.
The last three meetings in Poland in the last eight years have all ended in draws, a result that would not particularly favour either side on Saturday.
Poland's only chance of keeping their qualifying campaign alive is if they win. A draw would leave them with the remotest mathematical chance of finishing second while if they lose they are out.

Coach Antoni Piechniczek, under mounting pressure, is expected to play with an attacking formation, with two strikers rather than the one he employed in their last qualifier, a 3-0 defeat to group leaders Italy.

Although the dangerous Marek Citko will be missing from the attack with a torn achilles tendon which will sideline him for three months, Piechniczek is expected to start with Jacek Dembinski and Andrzej Juskowiak up front now that Juskowiak has recovered from an ankle injury.
Piotr Nowak, Poland's influential midfielder has also recovered from injury and should play.

Hoddle paid the Poles a compliment when he said: "They will be very difficult to beat. They are strong defensively and well organised and the crowd here get behind the team and can make it very intimidating for the opposition.
"We played our worst game since I took over against Poland at Wembley last year and still managed to win 2-1. I hope we get the same result tomorrow."
England (from): David Seaman; Gary Neville, Gareth Southgate, Sol Campbell, Stuart Pearce, David Beckham, Paul Ince, David Batty, Paul Gascoigne, Graeme Le Saux, Teddy Sheringham, Alan Shearer.

Poland (probable): Andrzej Wozniak; Radoslaw Kaluzny, Jacek Zielinski, Marek Jozwiak, Tomasz Waldoch, Krzysztof Bukalski, Piotr Nowak, Slawimir Majak, Adam Ledworn, Andrzej Juskowiak, Jacek Dembinski.
